audit_findings.title: Finance-lease-funded equipment may bypass the owner-earnings reinvestment charge
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 finance-lease additions $15.896m, principal payments $8.372m, and year-end liability $31.058m; principal payments equal 35.2% of $23.8m anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: If depreciation is added back while neither finance-lease asset additions nor principal payments are deducted, OE omits the cash cost of equipment reinvestment; an uncaptured liability would also affect the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Any financing leases executed for the acquisition of right-of-use machinery and equipment assets are presented in the supplemental disclosures of non-cash information on the statement of cash flows.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate substantial finance-lease investment and cash principal payments, but the supplied valuation does not establish their treatment in OE. The amounts are large relative to anchor OE and could materially reduce every scenario.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each OE year to finance-lease additions, depreciation, and principal payments; deduct a non-duplicative maintenance-equivalent charge and rerun all scenarios, and confirm whether the $31.058m liability is already represented through equity-level OE treatment.

audit_findings.title: The Karta stake appears to be added gross while its $7.5 million acquisition obligation is omitted
audit_findings.magnitude: $7.5m initial contingent consideration, equal to $0.59 per diluted share and 2.0% of $366m base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds the Karta investment but may omit the associated contingent-consideration claim; future rebates could also reduce OE if not already captured.
audit_findings.evidence: The total consideration for the transaction was $ 10.0 million, with $ 2.5 million paid in cash upon closing, and the remaining $ 7.5 million recorded as contingent consideration, which is included in “Other long-term liabilities” on the Company’s consolidated balance sheet.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that only $2.5m of the $10.0m consideration was paid at closing and that $7.5m was recorded as a liability. A full $7.5m omission exceeds the approximately $6.36m difference between base value and market capitalization at $28.24, so it can change the base valuation conclusion. The latest Karta-specific balance remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 30, 2026 Karta contingent-consideration balance and map it against stakes_net and forecast rebate cash flows; deduct the outstanding claim once, then rerun the bridge and per-share values.

audit_findings.title: Karta is potentially counted both in owner earnings and as a separate bridge asset
audit_findings.magnitude: filed equity-method losses of $0.134m in FY2025 and $0.403m in the first six months of 2026; treatment in OE is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding the stake in the bridge requires purging equity-method income or loss from OE; otherwise affiliate losses depress OE while future affiliate profits would inflate OE and duplicate bridge value.
audit_findings.evidence: Under the equity method, the investment is initially recognized at cost, and the carrying amount is subsequently adjusted to recognize the Company’s share of the investee’s net income or loss, which is recognized in the condensed consolidated statement of operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that equity-method losses enter reported net income, but the record does not show whether they were removed in the OE calculation. The recorded 2025 loss is only 0.6% of anchor OE, but future affiliate results and their valuation effect cannot be established from the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile historical OE to the equity-method line, remove all Karta income or losses when the stake is separately valued, and rerun if the reconciliation shows any retained amount.

audit_findings.title: All cash is treated as distributable despite stated operating and financing needs
audit_findings.magnitude: $21.368m of cash added, equal to $1.68 per diluted share and 5.8% of $366m base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds cash dollar-for-dollar; any minimum operating, working-capital, lease, interest, or debt-service cash is not excess and should not be added separately.
audit_findings.evidence: Although we can provide no assurances, we believe that our cash flows from operations, combined with our current cash levels and our senior secured revolving credit facility (the “ABL Revolver”) with available borrowing capacity of $74.7 million as of December 31, 2025, will be adequate to fund debt service requirements and provide cash, as required, to support our ongoing operations, capital expenditures, lease obligations and working capital needs.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing does not demonstrate that all cash is trapped or required, especially given $92.3m of revolver availability, but it also does not establish that the full balance is distributable. Removing more than approximately $6.36m would erase the base scenario's premium to the market price, so the unresolved excess-cash assumption is material.
audit_findings.action: Calculate minimum cash from monthly liquidity, working-capital seasonality, covenant headroom, lease payments, and scheduled interest; add only the demonstrably excess amount and rerun the bridge.

audit_findings.title: The latest anchor retains material acquisition and integration costs
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.0m pretax, equal to 25.2% of $23.8m anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: A genuinely non-recurring transaction or integration expense retained in net income lowers anchor OE and therefore operating PV and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Additionally, the Company incurred $ 6.0 million of acquisition and integration costs during the year ended December 31, 2025, which are presented in “Selling, general, and administrative” expenses in the Company’s consolidated statement of operations and comprehensive income.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates $6.0m of 2025 acquisition and integration expense and states that integration costs may continue. The supplied record does not establish whether OE removed it or what portion is genuinely non-recurring, but the amount is large enough to materially change value if an adjustment is warranted.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $6.0m to anchor OE, separate transaction-only costs from recurring integration and acquisition-program spending, calculate the supported after-tax adjustment, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The anchor year contains a prospective revenue-recognition timing transition
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 consolidated revenue was reduced by $10.1m; associated profit, working-capital, and OE effects are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The prospective shift from over-time to point-in-time recognition can move revenue, profit, and working capital between periods; using the transition year as perpetual OE may embed a temporary shortfall.
audit_findings.evidence: Effective prospectively beginning in the second quarter of 2025, the Company began recognizing revenue for these contracts at a point in time, typically upon shipment or customer acceptance.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing quantifies the 2025 revenue timing reduction but not its profit or OE effect. First-half 2026 comparisons show that the accounting change affected reported period-to-period revenue, yet the record cannot determine how much deferred 2025 economics reversed, its margin, or whether OE working-capital adjustments already offset it.
audit_findings.action: Build a contract-level roll-forward of affected work in process through 2026, quantify gross profit and cash-working-capital effects, reconcile them to 2025 OE, and rerun only for any demonstrated timing distortion not already recovered in OE.
